name: Basmati Rice
intro: Basmati rice is recognised for its slender grain, delicate aroma and pronounced elongation after cooking. Patel Impex coordinates Indian sourcing, buyer-defined processing and export packing for importers, distributors and food-service buyers.
overview: Available programs can cover raw, steam, white sella and golden sella processing. Variety, crop year, ageing, grain length, broken percentage and packing are confirmed against the buyer’s order before supply.
specs: Approximately 7.5–8.4 mm for selected long-grain lots
Raw, steam, white sella or golden sella
Final values confirmed by lot specification or certificate of analysis
physical: White to creamy-white or golden, depending on processing, with a slender shape and characteristic aroma. Properly cooked grains are expected to elongate and remain comparatively separate.
processing: Paddy is cleaned, de-stoned, milled and graded. Depending on the order, it may be steamed or parboiled before milling, then colour-sorted and inspected. Ageing and polish are agreed with the buyer.
packaging: Common options include food-grade PP, non-woven, jute and laminated retail bags in buyer-agreed sizes. Private-label artwork and packing configuration are subject to order review.
storage: Store sealed bags in a cool, dry, clean and pest-controlled area, protected from moisture, odours and direct sunlight.
quality: Quality is managed against an approved pre-shipment specification. Numeric values shown here are indicative trade ranges, not fixed claims for every lot.
faq: Which Basmati varieties can I request?
Common enquiries include 1121, 1509, 1401, Pusa and Traditional Basmati. Availability depends on crop and order timing.
Can processing be selected?
Yes. Raw, steam, white sella and golden sella options can be discussed.
Are specifications fixed?
No. Grain length, moisture, broken percentage and other parameters are confirmed for the contracted lot.

name: Non-Basmati Rice
eyebrow: Versatile rice for volume food programs
intro: Non-Basmati rice covers a broad range of Indian rice suited to everyday meals, wholesale channels and food processing. Patel Impex helps buyers define grain type, processing method, broken percentage and packing before sourcing.
overview: The range can include medium- and short-grain selections in raw, parboiled or white-rice form. Each programme is aligned to destination requirements and buyer-approved parameters.
specs: Raw, parboiled or polished white rice
physical: Mild to neutral aroma with white, translucent or lightly creamy grains according to variety and processing. Cooked texture can range from firm and separate to slightly soft.
processing: Rice is cleaned, de-stoned, milled, graded and colour-sorted. Parboiling, polishing and sortex selection are specified according to the required end use.
packaging: Food-grade PP, non-woven, jute or laminated bags in retail and bulk formats can be discussed. Final pack size and marking follow the purchase contract.
storage: Keep in a cool, dry, ventilated and pest-controlled warehouse. Protect bags from floor moisture, strong odours and direct sunlight.
quality: Indicative ranges support enquiry planning. Contract values, testing and tolerance are agreed for each product lot.
faq: How is Non-Basmati different from Basmati?
It generally has a milder aroma and different grain dimensions, making it suitable for high-volume everyday uses.
Can I request parboiled rice?
Yes. Raw and parboiled options can be discussed by variety.
Which parameters should an enquiry include?
State the variety, processing, grain length, broken percentage, moisture limit, quantity, destination and pack size.

name: Wheat Flour
intro: Wheat flour is milled to deliver the protein, ash, granulation and handling properties required by different food applications. Patel Impex coordinates flour sourcing for distributors, bakeries, food-service buyers and processors.
overview: Standard white flour programs may include all-purpose and baker’s flour profiles. Flour is not ready to eat and should be thoroughly cooked before consumption.
specs: Indicative range: approximately 9–13% by flour type
Varies by extraction and flour grade
Fine, uniform milling; buyer-defined where relevant
Final specification confirmed for each order
physical: Fine, free-flowing white to creamy powder. Colour, gluten strength, protein and water absorption vary with wheat blend and milling extraction.
processing: Wheat is cleaned and conditioned before roller milling. Bran and germ are separated for refined flour, then streams are blended to the required functional profile and sieved before packing.
packaging: Common formats include lined paper bags, woven PP bags and buyer-approved food-grade packs. Pack size, labels and palletisation are confirmed with the order.
storage: Store cool and dry in sealed packaging, away from moisture, pests and odorous materials. Use stock rotation and follow the lot’s stated best-before period.
quality: Protein and ash figures from source research describe common flour classes; PATEL IMPEX confirms actual lot values before shipment.
faq: Which flour is suitable for bread?
A baker’s flour with stronger gluten and a higher protein target is commonly selected.
Is raw flour ready to eat?
No. Flour should be thoroughly cooked before consumption.
Can protein be specified?
Yes. Share the target application and protein range with the enquiry.

name: Whole Wheat Flour
eyebrow: Whole-grain flour with bran and germ
intro: Whole wheat flour is milled from the complete wheat kernel, retaining bran, germ and endosperm. It offers a fuller flavour, darker appearance and different water absorption from refined wheat flour.
overview: Fine and coarser granulations can support flatbreads, bakery products and whole-grain formulations. Wheat selection and milling profile are matched to the intended application.
specs: Typically higher than refined flour; buyer-defined
Whole kernel: bran, germ and endosperm
physical: Cream to light brown flour with visible bran particles depending on granulation. It has a characteristic wheat aroma and higher water absorption than many refined flours.
processing: Cleaned wheat is conditioned and milled while retaining the whole-kernel components. Streams are recombined and sieved to achieve the required granulation.
packaging: Food-grade lined bags or woven PP sacks are available in buyer-agreed retail and bulk formats.
storage: Because whole wheat flour contains the germ, careful cool, dry storage and stock rotation are important. Keep sealed and protected from heat, humidity and pests.
quality: Specifications are agreed per contract. Product suitability should be validated in the buyer’s own formulation and process.
faq: How does whole wheat flour differ from refined flour?
It retains bran and germ, giving a darker colour, fuller flavour and different functional behaviour.
Can granulation be selected?
Fine and coarser profiles can be discussed.
What information should I provide?
Tell us the end use, target protein, granulation, quantity, destination and packing requirement.

name: Cumin
eyebrow: Whole Indian cumin for spice buyers
intro: Cumin, also known as jeera, is the dried seed of Cuminum cyminum. Its warm aroma and earthy flavour make it a core ingredient for spice blending, seasoning and food processing.
overview: Whole cumin can be sourced in buyer-defined cleanliness and purity grades. Crop, origin, seed appearance, volatile-oil expectations and residue requirements should be stated in the enquiry.
physical: Elongated, ridged seeds with brownish-yellow to darker brown colour and a strong, warm, characteristic aroma. Natural crop variation is expected.
processing: Seeds are cleaned to remove dust, stones and extraneous matter, then graded and optionally sortex-cleaned. Grinding is normally completed closer to use to protect aroma.
packaging: Common export formats include lined PP or jute bags and cartons in buyer-agreed weights. Retail packing can be reviewed separately.
storage: Keep sealed in a cool, dry and well-ventilated space, protected from moisture, heat, sunlight and strong odours.
quality: Purity and chemistry values are indicative. Residue, microbiological and destination-specific requirements must be agreed and tested for the contracted lot.
faq: Is jeera the same as cumin?
Yes. Jeera is the commonly used Indian name for cumin seed.
Can sortex-cleaned cumin be requested?
Yes, subject to crop availability and the agreed specification.
Do you guarantee the indicative purity?
No. The final contracted purity is confirmed on the lot specification and supporting test documents.

name: Peanuts
eyebrow: Indian groundnut kernels for bulk buyers
intro: Peanuts, also called groundnuts, are kernels of Arachis hypogaea used in snacks, confectionery, oil milling and ingredient processing. Patel Impex sources Indian types according to size count, moisture, quality and destination controls.
overview: The range can include Bold, Java/Spanish and TJ selections. Raw kernel supply is planned against crop availability and buyer-defined food-safety criteria.
specs: Buyer-defined; common trade counts span roughly 40–100 kernels per ounce
Indicative target: up to 99% or buyer-defined
Destination-specific limit; confirmed by contracted testing
physical: Cream kernels with a reddish to pinkish skin, varying from large Bold kernels to smaller Java and TJ counts. Flavour becomes more pronounced after roasting.
processing: Pods are shelled, aspirated, cleaned and graded by size. Colour sorting and additional food-safety controls may be specified. No absolute “zero aflatoxin” or pathogen claim is made.
packaging: Common options include food-grade vacuum packs, lined woven sacks or cartons in buyer-agreed weights. Container configuration depends on pack and destination.
storage: Store cool, dry and protected from heat, humidity, pests and direct sunlight. Peanuts should be managed carefully to limit moisture uptake and rancidity.
quality: Aflatoxin, pesticide residue and microbiological limits are market-specific and must be agreed in the contract and verified for the shipment.
faq: Which peanut types are available?
Common Indian enquiries include Bold, Java/Spanish and TJ counts.
Can aflatoxin limits be specified?
Yes. State the destination and required limit so the testing plan can be reviewed.
Are the peanuts ready to eat?
Raw peanuts require appropriate processing or cooking before consumption.

name: Psyllium Seed
intro: Psyllium seed, also known as isabgol seed, is the whole seed of Plantago ovata. It is the agricultural raw material from which psyllium husk is mechanically separated.
overview: Seed lots can be discussed by purity, moisture, foreign matter and swelling index. Final parameters are aligned to the processor or buyer’s intended use.
physical: Small oval or boat-shaped seeds, generally pale to light brown, with a smooth appearance and mucilage-forming outer layer.
processing: Harvested seed is dried, mechanically cleaned, aspirated and graded. Further de-husking and milling are completed when producing husk or powder.
packaging: Common export formats include lined jute or PP bags in 25 kg or 50 kg sizes, with custom packing subject to review.
storage: Store sealed in a cool, dry, pest-controlled area away from heat, light and moisture.
quality: Indicative values are based on common trade descriptions. Contracted purity and swelling performance are confirmed for the supplied lot.
faq: Is Psyllium Seed the same as Psyllium Husk?
No. The seed is the whole agricultural product; husk is the fibre-rich outer seed coat separated during processing.
What should processors specify?
Purity, moisture, foreign matter, swelling index, quantity and packing are useful starting parameters.
Is the botanical identity Plantago ovata?
Yes, this product page concerns Plantago ovata psyllium.

name: Psyllium Husk
eyebrow: Fibre-rich husk for food and ingredient buyers
intro: Psyllium husk is the cleaned outer seed coat of Plantago ovata. It hydrates rapidly and forms a mucilaginous gel, making it useful as a dietary-fibre ingredient and functional binder.
overview: Husk grades are commonly differentiated by purity, colour, swelling volume, ash and microbiological parameters. PATEL IMPEX confirms the buyer’s intended use and required test plan before supply.
specs: Whole or minimally broken husk flakes
physical: Lightweight, thin, translucent flakes with white to pale buff colour, a faint characteristic odour and strong water-binding behaviour.
processing: Cleaned psyllium seed is mechanically milled or de-husked, then the lighter husk is separated by controlled air and sieving systems. The product is graded and tested before packing.
packaging: Typical formats include lined HDPE, laminated paper or food-grade bags. Common weights include 10 kg, 15 kg, 25 kg and 50 kg; final format is buyer-agreed.
storage: Preserve in well-closed packaging in a cool, dry, pest-controlled space. Protect this hygroscopic product from moisture and insect exposure.
quality: Grade names do not by themselves prove pharmacopoeial compliance. Any USP, EP, IP, organic or microbiological requirement must be expressly contracted and documented.
faq: What determines Psyllium Husk grade?
Purity, colour, swelling volume, ash, foreign matter and microbiological requirements commonly define the grade.
Is every 99% grade pharmaceutical grade?
No. Compendial compliance requires the applicable test methods and documentation, not purity alone.
Can packaging be customised?
Yes, subject to product protection, quantity and destination requirements.
